title: Apoc 22:11: justify means grow more just, not bare declaration
source_text: XVI. Inter Protestantes autem pauci reperiuntur qui non agnoscant verbum justificandi sensum forensem non habere Apoc. 22. vers. 11. Qui justus est, justificetur adhuc; & qui sanctus est, sanctificetur adhuc. Ubi satis apparet, ex mente Spiritus Sancti, justificare illic non esse justum declarari, imo nec simpliciter ex injusto justum fieri, sed ex jam pio justoque magis justum ac pium: adeoque justificari, eo loco significat in pietate & justitia pergere, progredi, atque augescere.
pass_a_gloss: But among Protestants few are found who do not acknowledge that the verb of justifying does not have a forensic sense in Apoc. 22:11. He that is just, let him be justified still; and he that is holy, let him be sanctified still. Where it sufficiently appears, from the mind of the Holy Spirit, that to justify there is not to be declared just, nay nor simply to be made just out of unjust, but out of one already pious and just to become more just and pious: and so to be justified in that place signifies to continue, progress, and increase in piety and righteousness.
pass_b_english: Almost all Protestants deny forensic sense at Rev 22:11.
Justify there = grow more just/pious from already just—progress in righteousness.

lemmas.gloss: to continue in piety and righteousness
